After his parlay with Renly, Stannis states that the men fighting for Renly are the least honourable of all. He argues that good men will fight and die for him, and for Joffrey, genuinely believing each of them to be the true king. Good men will fight and die for Robb Stark and for Balon Greyjoy, genuinely believing their respective claims to be valid. But, according to Stannis, every man who fights for Renly knows from the start they are not fighting for the true king, just the a man who wanted it.

I don't want to jump on the recent Stannis hate wagon, but isn't that completely hypocritical of him, considering he fought for Robert, knowing full well he wasn't the king by right of succession? And before you respond that Stan only fought for Robert because Robert was his older brother, his liege lord, the head of his house, etc., is that not also true for the vast, vast majority of Renly's army? There might be a couple dozen, maybe 50 at the most, lords or lessor lords in Renly's forces who actually chose to serve Renly. As for the thousands of rank and file soldiers, are they not just obeying the commands of their leige lord, or the head of their household/family? Why is Stannis fighting against the king because he was sworn to someone else ok, but if anyone else does it they're dishonourable?

During Robert's rebellion the alternative was the Mad King who was burning people and doing all sorts of crazy stuff and it was decided by the rebelling houses they wouldn't put up with it anymore. So Stannis had to decide between his moral obligation to his king and his moral obligation to his brother's rebellion that wanted to replace a tyrant king. Renly was deciding against his moral obligation to his older brothers succession and his selfish desire to be king. Stannis had to choose between two rights, Renly had to choose between one right and wrong and he chose the wrong.
I agree with everything here. I blame Renly for (almost) everything bad that happens in Westeros, and it's all because he wanted to play king.

To add on to that, the heir Rhaegar wasn't looking to promising either by kidnapping the daughter of the lord of the North. Really the future under the Targs didn't seem good and Westeros would be ruled by tyrants. Also, Robert and his brothers are 1/4 Targaryen, so they did indeed have a claim to the throne.
